title: Facing Finitude
coreMove: Treat a finite calendar as the form meaning takes: choose the good that deserves your hours, and let the other real goods remain unchosen.

exampleSpecs.audience: Honore, a seminar leader handling a difficult source without flattening it
exampleSpecs.stakes: The group may either dismiss the material too quickly or let the difficulty become an excuse for admiration.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the scandal and the useful existential claim without treating either as the whole lesson.

exampleSpecs.audience: Craig, a parent deciding how much of a rare trip to protect
exampleSpecs.stakes: A reachable work request threatens to convert a finite family afternoon into ordinary remote labor.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Make temporary family time visible through Hägglund's Baltic coast and glacier retreat example.

exampleSpecs.audience: Sawyer, a caregiver absorbing bad news without turning it into a slogan
exampleSpecs.stakes: The family needs clarity and presence, not a cheerful story about growth through suffering.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show mortality making ordinary care sharper without suggesting the diagnosis is good news.

exampleSpecs.audience: Eitan, an editor noticing how sudden violence changes ordinary obligation
exampleSpecs.stakes: A routine day can stay automatic or become a reminder that any menu of choices was never owed.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn Cain's Toronto reaction into gratitude for having choices at all.

exampleSpecs.audience: Brett, a lead cutting a plan that has become a fantasy of doing everything
exampleSpecs.stakes: The team can keep every attractive promise on paper, or choose which promise will actually receive time.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use finitude as meaning to show that a real yes excludes other worthwhile projects.

exampleSpecs.audience: Florentine, an independent designer protecting a seasonal family visit
exampleSpecs.stakes: A lucrative contract would crowd out the one week that gives the season its human center.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Let the Baltic vacation case show why a temporary season can deserve protection.
